title: Digital Skills: Google Classroom and the Cloud

pages.c15-p01: Explain what the cloud is and compare saving work in cloud storage with saving it on a device
pages.c15-p02: Sign in to Google Classroom with your school account, join a class with a class code and use the Stream, Classwork and People pages
pages.c15-p03: Find, open and hand in an assignment, unsubmit work if needed, and use private and class comments correctly
pages.c15-p04: Use Google Drive to create folders, give files sensible names and organise your work
pages.c15-p05: Use Google Docs, Slides and Sheets for the right tasks, and explain autosave and version history
pages.c15-p06: Share a file with the right permission (viewer, commenter or editor) and use comments and suggesting mode
pages.c15-p07: Compare synchronous and asynchronous collaboration tools and work on a shared document responsibly
pages.c15-p08: Upload files to Drive and Classroom, recognise common file types and convert between them
pages.c15-p09: Use the To-do list, calendar and notifications to stay organised and meet deadlines
pages.c15-p10: Communicate appropriately for your audience, and act as a responsible digital citizen: avoiding plagiarism, protecting personal data and keeping your account secure
pages.c15-p11: Solve common problems with Google Classroom and Drive, such as missing assignments, failed uploads and the wrong account

q.q: What is cloud storage?
o: Saving files on a provider's servers, reached over the internet
Saving files on the hard drive inside your own laptop
Saving files on a USB stick kept in your school bag
Saving files in a folder on the computer's desktop
q.why: Cloud storage keeps files on remote servers that you reach over the internet.

q.q: Where are files in the cloud actually stored?
o: In satellites orbiting the Earth
Inside your web browser
On the router in your house
On servers in data centres
q.why: The cloud is really servers in large buildings called data centres.

q.q: Which of these is an example of local storage?
o: A folder in Google Drive
An attachment in Google Classroom
A USB stick plugged into the school computer
A shared folder in OneDrive
q.why: A USB stick is storage attached to the device you are using.

q.q: Which word describes storage that is somewhere other than the device you are using?
o: Local storage
Remote storage
Internal storage
Primary storage
q.why: Remote storage is not inside the device, e.g. cloud storage.

q.q: Ciara's laptop is stolen, but all her homework was saved in Google Drive. What happens to her work?
o: It is safe: she can sign in on another device and open it
It is lost, because the files were on the stolen laptop
It is safe only if she had also printed every file
It is lost unless the thief signs out of her account
q.why: Cloud files stay on the provider's servers, so any device can reach them.

q.q: Which is a genuine disadvantage of cloud storage?
o: Files can only be opened on the device that created them
Only one person can ever look at a file at the same time
Files are deleted every night unless you print them
Anyone who learns your password can reach your files from anywhere
q.why: Cloud security depends heavily on your password.

q.q: Why do data centres have an environmental cost?
o: Every file has to be printed on paper and stored in boxes
Data centres burn old computers to make room for new ones
Servers run all day and need cooling, using electricity and often water
Each saved file permanently drains your own phone battery
q.why: Running and cooling servers uses lots of electricity and water.

q.q: Google Docs runs in your web browser without being installed. This is an example of:
o: Local storage
A data centre
An operating system
Cloud computing
q.why: Software that runs on remote servers over the internet is cloud computing.

q.q: Erin says, 'My work is in the cloud, so I can never lose any of it.' What is the best reply?
o: Not quite: if you delete or overwrite it, the cloud saves that mistake too
Correct: cloud providers stop you from deleting anything at all
Not quite: cloud files are deleted automatically after one week
Correct: cloud files are copied onto every computer in the school
q.why: The cloud saves every change, including mistakes, though version history can help.

q.q: Which page of a Google Classroom class shows announcements from your teacher?
o: Classwork
People
To-do
Stream
q.why: The Stream is the class noticeboard.

q.q: Which page of a class lists all the assignments and materials grouped into topics?
o: Stream
People
Classwork
Calendar
q.why: Classwork holds all the work, organised by topic.

q.q: What does the People page of a class show?
o: Every assignment that is still missing
The files shared with you in Drive
The marks for each pupil in the class
The teachers and classmates in the class
q.why: People lists the teachers and pupils.

q.q: What is a class code?
o: Your C2k password for logging in at school
A number given to each assignment you hand in
A 6 to 8 character code used to join a class
The name of the folder your work is saved in
q.why: You type the class code once to join the class.

q.q: What is the school Google account address for a C2k pupil with the username jsmith123?
o: jsmith123@gmail.com
jsmith123@classroom.com
jsmith123@myschool.co.uk
jsmith123@c2ken.net
q.why: C2k Google accounts are username@c2ken.net.

q.q: Oisín types the class code exactly, but Classroom will not let him join. What should he check first?
o: Whether he is signed in with his school account
Whether his file names are sensible
Whether his Drive Bin has been emptied
Whether the class has posted on the Stream
q.why: A personal or family account is the most common reason a correct code fails.

q.q: Which of these would be an example of 'material' on the Classwork page?
o: A homework that must be turned in by Friday
A multiple-choice question to answer
A comment from a classmate about the homework
A set of notes to read, with nothing to hand in
q.why: Material is notes, links or videos with nothing to hand in.

q.q: Where should Callum look to see who else is in 8C ICT?
o: The Classwork page
The People page
The To-do list
His Google Drive
q.why: People shows the class members.

q.q: How often do you need to enter a class code for a class?
o: Every time you open the class
Once, when you first join
Once a week, on Mondays
Every time you turn in work
q.why: After joining, the class appears on every device you sign in to.

q.q: A class code is 'Ab3xQ9'. Grace types 'ab3xq9'. Why might this fail?
o: Codes must always be typed in capital letters only
Codes should be entered with the capitals exactly as given
Codes can only contain numbers, not letters
Codes need a space between the letters and numbers
q.why: Google says to enter capital letters exactly as given.

q.q: What does clicking Turn in do?
o: Deletes the assignment from your To-do list
Hands in your work so the teacher can mark it
Shares your work with the whole class
Moves the due date back by one day
q.why: Turn in hands the work in.

q.q: Jack attached his work to the assignment and closed the page. Why does his teacher see it as not handed in?
o: He used a private comment
He named the file sensibly
He opened it from the Stream
He never clicked Turn in
q.why: Attaching is not the same as turning in.

q.q: What does Unsubmit do?
o: Sends your work to a different class
Permanently deletes your work
Takes back your work so you can change it
Marks the work as late automatically
q.why: Unsubmit returns the work to you so you can edit it.

q.q: After unsubmitting and fixing her work, what must Niamh do?
o: Click Turn in again
Nothing: it is handed in automatically
Email the file to the teacher instead
Post the file as a class comment
q.why: Unsubmitted work does not count until you turn it in again.

q.q: Who can read a private comment on an assignment?
o: Everyone in the class
Only you and your teacher
Only the other pupils
Anyone with the class code
q.why: Private comments are between you and your teacher.

q.q: Who can read a class comment?
o: Only you and your teacher
Everyone in the class
Only your teacher
Only the person you reply to
q.why: Class comments are public to the class.

q.q: Grace wants to tell her teacher she was off sick and needs more time. What should she use?
o: A class comment on the Stream post
A comment in a shared group document
A note in the assignment's file name
A private comment on the assignment
q.why: Personal matters go in a private comment.

q.q: An assignment has nothing to attach. What does the button say instead of Turn in?
o: Unsubmit
Return
Mark as done
Submit late
q.why: With nothing to attach, the button is Mark as done.

q.q: Ruairí turned in his work on time, then unsubmitted it after the due date to fix one word, and turned it in again. How will it show?
o: Turned in on time, because the first turn-in still counts
Missing, because unsubmitted work can never be turned in again
Turned in late, because it was turned in again after the due date
Returned, because his teacher has to mark it again
q.why: Turning in again after the due date counts as late.

q.q: An assignment says 'Make a copy for each student'. What does this mean for you?
o: You must make a copy and email it to the teacher
Every pupil edits the same single file together
You get your own copy of the file to work in
You can only view the file and cannot edit it
q.why: Classroom makes a personal copy for each pupil.

q.q: Which is the best file name for a Geography project on Lough Erne?
o: Untitled document
Geography Lough Erne Project
Copy of project
my work final FINAL
q.why: It says the subject, the topic and what it is.

q.q: Where in Google Drive do files that other people share with you appear?
o: Shared with me
My Drive
Bin
Starred
q.why: Shared files appear in Shared with me.

q.q: How long do deleted files stay in the Google Drive Bin before they are deleted for good?
o: 7 days
30 days
24 hours
1 year
q.why: Files in the Bin are permanently deleted after 30 days.

q.q: Which steps create a new folder in Google Drive?
o: New, then New folder
Share, then New folder
File, then Version history
Bin, then Restore
q.why: New > New folder creates a folder.

q.q: What does Google Classroom automatically create in your Drive?
o: A copy of every file your teacher has ever made
A folder of all your classmates' work
A Classroom folder with a folder for each class
A backup of your C2k email inbox
q.why: Classroom makes a Classroom folder with one folder per class.

q.q: What manages the files saved locally on a Windows laptop?
o: Google Classroom
The data centre
The class code
The operating system
q.why: The operating system keeps track of files, folders and who can open them.

q.q: Jack deleted a folder called ICT. What has happened to the files inside it?
o: They were deleted too and are in the Bin
They were moved to My Drive automatically
They were sent to his teacher
Nothing: deleting a folder never affects files
q.why: Deleting a folder deletes everything inside it.

q.q: Which is an example of a sustainable digital habit?
o: Uploading the same video several times to be safe
Keeping every blurry photo in case you need it
Attaching a copy of a file to twenty separate emails
Deleting old duplicate files you will never use
q.why: Fewer stored files means less energy used in data centres.

q.q: Why is 'Copy of Copy of Science' a poor file name?
o: It is too short for Google Drive
Google Drive cannot store copies
It does not say what the file is about
Copies cannot be handed in
q.why: A name should describe the contents.

q.q: Which Google app is best for writing a letter to a local councillor?
o: Google Sheets
Google Docs
Google Slides
Google Forms
q.why: Docs is the word processor.

q.q: Which Google app is best for a table of rugby scores with an average?
o: Google Sheets
Google Docs
Google Slides
Google Drive
q.why: Sheets is a spreadsheet for numbers and calculations.

q.q: Which Google app is most like Microsoft PowerPoint?
o: Google Slides
Google Docs
Google Sheets
Google Forms
q.why: Slides is for presentations, like PowerPoint.

q.q: What is autosave?
o: The file is saved when you click the Save button
Every change is saved automatically as you work
A backup made by your teacher once a week
A copy saved to the desktop when you close it
q.why: Google files save each change automatically.

q.q: What is version history?
o: A list of every file you have ever deleted
A record of earlier versions of a file that can be restored
The history of websites visited in the browser
A record of which pupils have joined a class
q.why: Version history keeps earlier versions and shows who changed what.

q.q: Where do you find version history in Google Docs?
o: File > Version history > See version history
Insert > Version history > Restore
Share > Version history > Editors
Tools > Spelling and grammar > History
q.why: It is in the File menu.

q.q: Callum typed over two paragraphs of his essay last night and autosave saved it. What should he do?
o: Look for the missing paragraphs in the Bin
Restore an earlier version using version history
Unsubmit the essay to bring the text back
Switch to suggesting mode and undo it
q.why: Version history can bring back the earlier version.

q.q: Why should you not close a Google Doc immediately after the Wi-Fi drops?
o: Closing it while offline deletes the whole file
The file will be shared with everyone if you close it
Google Docs can only be closed when you are online
Your latest changes may not have been saved to Drive yet
q.why: Autosave needs a connection, so recent changes might not be saved.

q.q: In a group Doc, how could a teacher see that one pupil pasted in a large block of text at once?
o: By checking the Bin
By reading the class comments
By looking at version history
By looking at the file extension
q.why: Version history shows who changed what, and when.

q.q: Which permission lets someone only open and read a file?
o: Commenter
Editor
Owner
Viewer
q.why: Viewers can only read.

q.q: Which permission lets someone add comments and suggestions but not edit the text directly?
o: Commenter
Viewer
Editor
Owner
q.why: Commenters can comment and suggest.

q.q: Which permission lets someone change anything in a file?
o: Editor
Commenter
Viewer
Suggester
q.why: Editors can change everything.

q.q: Your granny wants to see your finished poster. Which permission is best?
o: Viewer
Editor
Commenter
Owner
q.why: Give the lowest permission needed: she only needs to look.

q.q: Your group of three is making one presentation together. Which permission should each member have?
o: Viewer
Commenter
Editor
None, just email copies
q.why: Everyone needs to change the slides.

q.q: What happens to your typing in suggesting mode?
o: It replaces the text straight away with no record
It appears in colour for the owner to accept or reject
It is emailed to the owner instead of being added
It is hidden until the document is turned in
q.why: Suggestions wait for the owner to decide.

q.q: Why is sharing with 'Anyone with the link' risky?
o: Anyone who gets the link, including strangers, can open it
It makes the file disappear after a single day
It turns every person who opens it into the owner
It stops the file from autosaving any changes
q.why: Links can be forwarded to anyone.

q.q: What does clicking Resolve on a comment do?
o: Deletes the text that the comment was on
Accepts every suggestion in the document
Sends the comment to your teacher privately
Marks it as dealt with and tidies it away
q.why: Resolving closes a comment once it is fixed.

q.q: Niamh wants Jack to check her story but not change her words without her agreeing. Which is the best choice?
o: Share as Commenter so his changes become suggestions
Share as Editor and ask him to be careful
Share as Viewer so he can suggest changes
Send him the password to her account
q.why: Commenters' edits appear as suggestions for her to accept or reject.

q.q: What does synchronous collaboration mean?
o: Working together at the same time
Working together at different times
Working alone and sharing at the end
Working only in the same classroom
q.why: Synchronous means in real time.

q.q: What does asynchronous collaboration mean?
o: Working together at the same time
Working without any internet access
Working only by video call
Working together at different times
q.why: Asynchronous means not at the same time.

q.q: Which is an example of synchronous collaboration?
o: Leaving comments for others to read later
Adding photos to a shared folder all week
Sending an email that is read the next day
A video call to plan a group project
q.why: A video call happens in real time.

q.q: Which is an example of asynchronous collaboration?
o: Adding research to a shared Drive folder during the week
Three pupils typing in the same Doc at once
Talking through a plan on a video call
Chatting live while co-editing a Slides file
q.why: Each person adds to the shared folder when it suits them.

q.q: Oisín leaves a comment on Sunday and Erin replies on Monday. This is:
o: Synchronous, because they use the same document
Synchronous, because both use Google Docs
Asynchronous, because comments are private
Asynchronous, because they work at different times
q.why: Different times means asynchronous.

q.q: Which is an advantage of asynchronous collaboration?
o: Every question gets an instant answer
People can contribute whenever it suits them
Everyone must be online at the same time
Nobody needs to read anyone else's work
q.why: Flexibility is the main advantage.

q.q: Which is a disadvantage of synchronous collaboration?
o: It can be hard to find a time when everyone is free
Replies can take several days to arrive
Nobody can see the others' changes
It cannot be used for group projects
q.why: Everyone must be available at once.

q.q: In a group Doc, Callum thinks Grace's paragraph could be better. What is the responsible thing to do?
o: Delete her paragraph and write his own version
Copy her paragraph into a new file of his own
Add a comment or suggestion for Grace to decide
Change her permission to Viewer so she stops editing
q.why: Comments and suggestions keep Grace in control of her section.

q.q: A group project uses a video call on Monday, then shared folder uploads during the week. Which statement is correct?
o: It uses only synchronous collaboration
It uses only asynchronous collaboration
It uses both synchronous and asynchronous collaboration
It uses neither type of collaboration
q.why: The call is synchronous; the shared folder is asynchronous.

q.q: What does uploading a file mean?
o: Copying it from your device to the cloud
Copying it from the cloud to your device
Changing it from one file type to another
Deleting it from your device to save space
q.why: Upload means sending a file up to the cloud.

q.q: What does the extension .docx tell you?
o: It is a PDF document
It is a PowerPoint presentation
It is a JPG photograph
It is a Microsoft Word document
q.why: .docx is a Word document.

q.q: What does the extension .pptx tell you?
o: It is an Excel spreadsheet
It is a Word document
It is a PNG image
It is a PowerPoint presentation
q.why: .pptx is a PowerPoint presentation.

q.q: Why might a teacher ask for finished work as a PDF?
o: It is the only file type Google Drive can store
It looks the same on every device and is hard to change
It lets the whole class edit the work together
It makes the file larger so it is easier to read
q.why: PDFs keep their layout and are hard to edit.

q.q: How do you attach a file from your laptop to an assignment?
o: Share, then Editor
New, then New folder
File, then Version history
Add or create, then File
q.why: Add or create > File uploads from your device.

q.q: How do you save a Google Doc as a Word file for someone who uses Microsoft Word?
o: File > Version history > Microsoft Word
Share > Editor > Microsoft Word (.docx)
File > Download > Microsoft Word (.docx)
Insert > File > Microsoft Word (.docx)
q.why: File > Download lets you choose Word format.

q.q: A 40 MB file is uploaded at 8 Mbps. How long does it take?
o: 5 seconds
320 seconds
40 seconds
48 seconds
q.why: 40 x 8 = 320 megabits; 320 / 8 = 40 seconds.

q.q: A 300 MB video is uploaded at 12 Mbps. How long does it take?
o: 25 seconds
2400 seconds
3600 seconds
200 seconds
q.why: 300 x 8 = 2400 megabits; 2400 / 12 = 200 seconds.

q.q: A pupil works out 100 MB at 10 Mbps as 100 / 10 = 10 seconds. What mistake did they make?
o: They should have multiplied 100 by 10 instead of dividing
They forgot to multiply the megabytes by 8 to get megabits
They should have divided the 10 by 100 instead
They forgot to divide the answer by 60 to get seconds
q.why: Sizes are in megabytes and speeds in megabits: 100 x 8 / 10 = 80 seconds.

q.q: Which To-do tab shows work past its due date that has not been turned in?
o: Assigned
Done
Missing
Returned
q.why: Missing means past the due date and not turned in.

q.q: Which To-do tab shows work you still have to do?
o: Assigned
Missing
Done
Stream
q.why: Assigned lists work still to do.

q.q: What does the To-do list gather together?
o: Only work from one class
Only work that has been marked
Work from all your classes
Only files shared with you
q.why: To-do collects work from every class.

q.q: What is a notification?
o: A comment that only your teacher can read
A code used to join a Classroom class
An alert telling you something has happened
A record of earlier versions of a file
q.why: Notifications alert you to new work, replies and returned work.

q.q: Where can you see your work placed on its due dates week by week?
o: The Classroom calendar
The People page
The Bin in Drive
Version history
q.why: The Calendar page shows work on its due date.

q.q: Grace finished her homework but it still sits under Assigned. What is the most likely reason?
o: Her teacher has not set a due date
She was signed in to her school account
She gave her file a sensible name
She did not click Turn in
q.why: Work stays in Assigned until it is turned in.

q.q: Jack has a Missing homework, one due tomorrow and one due next week. What should he do first?
o: The one due next week, because it is biggest
The Missing homework and the one due tomorrow
Nothing until his teacher sends a reminder
Whichever is in the subject he likes most
q.why: Late work and the nearest deadline come first.

q.q: What does 'plan backwards from the due date' mean?
o: Start the work on the day it is due
Decide when to finish, then work out when you must start
Hand in the work before reading the task
Do last week's homework before this week's
q.why: Work back from the deadline to set start and finish times.

q.q: Erin gets too many Classroom emails and wants to stop missing important ones. What is the best action?
o: Ignore every email from Google Classroom
Leave all the classes she gets emails from
Ask a friend to read her emails for her
Change her notification settings to keep the important ones
q.why: Adjust settings so the important alerts still arrive.

q.q: Which private comment is the most suitable to send to a teacher?
o: hey wat r we meant 2 do?? wasnt in lol
WHERE IS THE HOMEWORK I CANT FIND IT
send me the work pls i need it now
Hello Mr Butler, I was absent. Which worksheet should I do? Thanks, Erin
q.why: Polite, clear and signed suits a teacher.

q.q: Choosing how to write depending on who will read it is following a:
o: Communication protocol for the audience
Sharing permission for the document
Version history for the message
Class code for the conversation
q.why: Protocols are agreed rules of communication suited to the audience.

q.q: What is plagiarism?
o: Sharing a document with a classmate
Downloading your work as a PDF
Commenting on a friend's document
Passing off someone else's work as your own
q.why: Plagiarism is presenting others' work as yours.

q.q: How can you use information from a website in a project without plagiarising?
o: Put it in your own words and credit the source
Copy it exactly but change the font
Copy it exactly and put it in bold
Ask a friend to copy it in for you
q.why: Rewrite it and say where it came from.

q.q: Which of these is personal data?
o: The name of a school subject
A classmate's home address
A class code for ICT
The title of a homework
q.why: It identifies and locates a living person.

q.q: Which law controls how personal data is used in the UK?
o: The Copyright Act
The Freedom of Information Act
UK GDPR
The Online Safety Act
q.why: UK GDPR, with the Data Protection Act 2018, covers personal data.

q.q: A group Sheet lists everyone's phone numbers and addresses and is shared with anyone with the link. What is the main problem?
o: The Sheet will use too much storage space in Google Drive
Phone numbers cannot be typed into Google Sheets cells
Personal data could be seen and misused by people who should not have it
The file name does not include the subject and topic
q.why: Personal data must be kept secure and only shared when needed.

q.q: Why should you never share your school password with a friend?
o: It would stop your class code from working
It would turn off autosave in Google Docs
They could read, change or hand in work as you
It would move your files into the Bin
q.why: Anyone with your password can act as you.

q.q: What should you always do before leaving a shared school computer?
o: Close the lid or turn off the screen
Sign out of Google and log off
Empty the Bin in Google Drive
Switch the document to suggesting mode
q.why: Signing out stops others using your account.

q.q: At home, Callum's school classes have all vanished from Classroom. What is the most likely cause?
o: His teacher has deleted all of his classes
His files have been moved into the Bin
He is signed in with the wrong Google account
His class code has run out after a week
q.why: The wrong account is the most common cause.

q.q: How can you check which account Google Classroom is using?
o: Open the People page of a class
Click your profile picture in the top right
Look in the Bin in Google Drive
Check the file extension of your work
q.why: The profile picture shows the signed-in account.

q.q: Ruairí cannot edit a document he has already turned in. What should he do to change it?
o: Delete it and upload a brand new copy to the Stream
Change the file to a PDF and then edit it
Unsubmit it, make the change, then turn it in again
Ask a friend to log in and change it for him
q.why: Turned-in work is locked until it is unsubmitted or returned.

q.q: A video will not finish uploading to an assignment. Which is NOT a sensible step?
o: Checking the internet connection
Clicking Turn in before the upload finishes
Waiting for the upload to complete
Making the video file smaller
q.why: Turning in early means the teacher may get nothing.

q.q: Grace's group document is missing a whole slide. Where should she look to get it back?
o: The People page
The class code
Version history
The To-do list
q.why: Version history can restore the deleted slide.

q.q: It is the night before the deadline and you still cannot upload your work. What is the best action?
o: Message your teacher before the deadline and say what you tried
Wait until next week and explain then
Ask a friend to sign in as you to upload it
Turn in an empty assignment to avoid Missing
q.why: Telling your teacher in time, with what you tried, is the responsible choice.

q.q: Classroom has frozen and buttons do nothing. What is a sensible first step?
o: Unsubmit every assignment you have
Refresh the page or close other tabs
Empty the Bin in Google Drive
Change all files to Viewer access
q.why: Refreshing or freeing up the browser fixes most freezes.

q.q: Which tip helps most on a shared family computer?
o: Leave your school account signed in for everyone
Use a separate browser profile or private window for school
Write your password on a note next to the screen
Use your parent's account to hand in work
q.why: A separate profile or private window keeps accounts apart.
